title: Machine learning predicts long-term sudden cardiac death from lipid and clinical markers
summary: In the prospective Chin-Shan community cohort (3172 participants, 74 sudden cardiac death events over a median 15.9 years), six machine learning models were built after Boruta feature preselection. Random forest had the best discrimination (AUC 0.824 internal, 0.815 external) and was the only model to significantly beat the Framingham Risk Score, with NPV above 99% in both. The external set is a geographic split of the same cohort, and the number of events is small.
ai_technology: Random forest selected among six models after Boruta preselection, interpreted with SHAP and deployed as a web calculator
organization: Taichung Veterans General Hospital; National Chung Hsing University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Geographically independent external validation within the same community cohort.
evidence.unknown: Performance in other populations; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts sudden cardiac death risk over long follow-up from ten selected predictors.
